Figure 10-1 MTV onboard electrical system outline Final Technical Report 38/57 10.2 CEC Test System The CEC Test System is the electrical infrastructure used to test the CEC from clients. It will be separated from the vessel's normal operation equipment, so a second pair of main switchboards and a secondary switchboard are proposed to power all the devices related to the testing campaign or those for which operation is not fully needed for the vessel operation. It would normally be isolated and not affect the MTV onboard electrical system. The system was designed with technical support from NREL. The CEC connection to the system is 690 V (3 phase) based, and the maximum allowed power output from the CEC is 700 kVA. ABB proposed the grid simulation system using low voltage industrial ACS880 drives. The proposed system consists of one common DC bus within the drive system (Figure 10-2). All the components required are coupled to the DC bus through a converter of various functions. For instance, the CEC couples to the DC bus through a grid simulator unit, the resistive load couples to the DC bus through a braking unit, and the battery storage is coupled to the DC bus through a DC/DC converter. The MTV system is coupled to this DC bus through a diode supply unit (this unit is operated only whenever necessary). Apart from the resistive and battery storages, the converters units are unified into one cabinet. Having the system coupled at a DC bus greatly reduces the complexity of the controls and coordination. Figure 10-2 DC Bus Architecture Final Technical Report 39/57 11 OCEAN AND RIVER OPERATIONS DESIGN The operations to be performed along the MTV lifecycle, especially those related to CEC testing, have been essential in defining the requirements and design of the MTV. Although each of the operations should be designed in detail (taking into account the conditions of the site and the available means, performing a risk analysis, and defining the necessary mitigation actions) during this phase of the project, the goal has been to demonstrate that these operations have been taken into account in the design and are feasible. The main operations considered during the design are: • MTV launching and decommissioning • Docking and boarding in harbor • CEC loading on MTV and connection • MTV transport • Internal mooring (onboard) deployment • External mooring installation • Jack-up system deployment • CEC testing In addition, several considerations have been made regarding the LRP procedures and safety measures taken during the design of the MTV. Final Technical Report 40/57 12 RISK REGISTER & FMEA The risk register lists all uncertain events that could positively or negatively impact project development. Each risk is analyzed regarding the severity of its implications and the expected frequency of its occurrence, providing a risk prioritization.
